entries.title: Drone delivery helps in Rwanda, but only so much

entries.title: Keeping cool without AC: Our readers share their tips

entries.title: In Nebraska, Americans begin to lose Medicaid under Trump's work rules

entries.title: Trump's claims of 250,000 non-U.S. citizens on voter rolls leave some states baffled
entries.snippet: Trump officials say they found 250,000 noncitizens on voter rolls in just four states. Those states don't know where the numbers came from, and some worry what the claims may portend for the midterms.

entries.title: Huge blankets of seaweed are smothering coastlines from the Caribbean to Mexico
entries.snippet: Some 27 million metric tons of self-sustaining sargassum have been recorded in the Atlantic, Caribbean and Gulf of Mexico in July, according to a report released Friday by the University of South Florida's Optical Oceanography Lab.

entries.title: U.S. will make visa bond program permanent, affecting mostly African countries
entries.snippet: A draft notice published Friday in the Federal Register says a nearly year-long review "provided sufficient data" to suggest the bond program effectively enforces compliance with visa conditions, and would be made permanent.

entries.title: Arizona, California and Nevada would share cuts under federal proposal for Colorado River
entries.snippet: The U.S. Bureau of Reclamation proposal spares four other states from facing mandatory cuts for now.

entries.title: Social media companies sued over deaths of 4 teens amid rising pressure over child safety
entries.snippet: The families of four teenagers who died by suicide are suing Meta, TikTok, Snapchat and YouTube over what they describe as "years of escalating harms" from using their platforms that eventually resulted in their deaths.

entries.title: What's in the proposed deal to disarm Hamas and withdraw Israeli forces from Gaza

entries.snippet: Spain is rushing troops and resources to one of its territories in North Africa, after tens of thousands of migrants crossed the border from Morocco into the small city of Ceuta. Geoff Bennett reports.

entries.title: Local arts groups that shape community culture face financial pressure
entries.snippet: Larger theater companies, venues and museums typically get more attention. But in cities and rural areas, it's smaller arts organizations that are closest to and address the needs of their communities. Now, many are struggling as they face economic pressures. Jeffrey Brown report

entries.title: Why states want to change 'Sell By' labels on food
entries.snippet: Changes are coming to the commonly used sell-by dates on groceries in at least one state. PBS News multiplatform reporter Tim McPhillips spoke to two experts to get their take on the food labels and how you can save both your food and your money.

entries.title: Marine Corps says F-35B jet crashed in California, pilot in stable condition after ejecting
entries.snippet: The U.S. Marine Corps says the pilot of an F-35B stealth fighter is expected to live after ejecting from the jet before it crashed in California. The jet went down Friday near the Miramar air base in San Diego.

entries.title: Authorities release early Nancy Guthrie ransom note, hoping someone recognizes writing style
entries.snippet: Authorities released an early ransom note in the investigation into the disappearance of Nancy Guthrie in hopes that someone will recognize the writing style. A second note released Friday indicated Guthrie died shortly after she was kidnapped.

entries.title: Most of the 60,000 migrants who crossed into territory of Ceuta have left voluntarily, Spain says
entries.snippet: Many young Moroccans who crossed into Ceuta told The Associated Press that they had hoped to find better work opportunities in Spain but were returning given the mayhem in Ceuta.

entries.title: Who is Kathryn Ruemmler? Former Obama White House attorney interviewed about Epstein emails
entries.snippet: Ruemmler called Epstein, whom she first met in 2014, a "masterful liar" in her opening remarks to the panel, adding that she didn't see evidence of criminal conduct by Epstein.

entries.title: Quake survivors in southwestern Japan sleep in cars in sweltering heat as death toll rises to 34
entries.snippet: Rescuers raced to find those still missing after the quake triggered a mall explosion, toppled a factory chimney and flattened homes.

entries.title: Hamas says it will disarm if Israel halts strikes and withdraws from Gaza, but obstacles remain
entries.snippet: Hamas said that laying down its heavy weapons, which would come later in the process, was contingent on the creation of a Palestinian state, something Israel's current government adamantly rejects.

entries.title: FIFA chief Infantino abandons World Cup sell-off plans after backlash
entries.snippet: Europe's governing body, UEFA, had threatened to boycott FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup, unless Gianni Infantino withdrew his plans to sell stakes in FIFA competitions to private equity investors.

entries.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak becomes world's second-largest ever
entries.snippet: DR Congo’s fast-spreading Ebola outbreak has exceeded 3,500 cases, overtaking the country’s deadliest epidemic and becoming the world’s second-largest ever. The Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccine or treatment.

entries.title: UK court allows plans for Chinese 'super' embassy to advance
entries.snippet: A court dismissed a legal challenge against Beijing's new embassy in London, which could become the largest in the UK. The case, brought by a neighborhood association, argued the embassy poses a security threat.

entries.title: Why Europe's wildfires are getting harder to stop
entries.snippet: Wildfires may start with a single spark, but experts say climate change, drought and decades of forest management decisions have created the conditions for Europe's biggest blazes.

entries.title: Sudan civil war: When drones strike the classroom
entries.snippet: Children in Sudan's besieged city of el-Obeid are afraid to go to school as drone attacks hit civilian infrastructure. Aid groups warn of a worsening humanitarian crisis.

entries.title: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
entries.snippet: From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

entries.title: Humanoid robots: Trump's latest China trade battle?
entries.snippet: The US has banned foreign-made humanoid robots, a market Chinese tech firms dominates. Although Washington cited national security risks, analysts think Donald Trump is buying time for US robot makers to catch up.

entries.title: Germany news: Unemployment tops 3 million as industry slumps
entries.snippet: Over three million people are currently unemployed in Germany, with 1.1 million drawing unemployment checks, authorities say. Also, sales of air conditioners have doubled as heat continues to crush cities.

entries.title: Eco wins: From death strip to nature haven and other green surprises
entries.snippet: A Cold War relic becomes a biodiversity haven, a Pokemon Go for trees and seagrass gets a second life. This week's eco wins come from some unexpected places.

entries.title: Small insects, big damage: The global ant trade is booming
entries.snippet: Legal or not, the trade in African ants bound for Europe is booming. What do hobbyists find appealing about these insects, and what risks does the trade pose to ecosystems, including power outages?

entries.title: India's 'Cockroach' protesters face ongoing legal pressure
entries.snippet: After forcing the resignation of India's education minister, student activists say a crackdown continues despite government promises to drop criminal cases against protesters.

entries.title: FIFA plans: Infantino under pressure as senior advisor quits
entries.snippet: After regional football federations condemned FIFA plans for private investment, Carlos Cordeiro, senior advisor to FIFA President Gianni Infantino, tendered his resignation.

entries.title: Ceuta: Spain says most migrants have returned to Morocco
entries.snippet: Spain's government said that an estimated 48,300 migrants were back in Morocco on Friday evening. Italy has temporarily suspended its Schengen free-travel pact with Spain. DW has more.

entries.title: German court rules that AI music firm Suno violated copyrights
entries.snippet: Germany's state-mandated licensing agency, GEMA, says the verdict has "global significance," as Suno is also directed to pay yet-to-be-quantified damages.

entries.title: Military flare-up between Houthis and Saudi Arabia challenges relative calm in Yemen
entries.snippet: Riyadh and Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels are on the brink of renewed conflict. Could war-ravaged Yemen be drawn into a wider Middle East war?

entries.title: Spain's PM visits Ceuta after thousands breached border
entries.snippet: Thousands of people continued pouring into Ceuta from Morocco during the night, after Spanish police lost control of the border. The head of the city government estimated that 60,000 people had entered.

entries.title: Dozens of miners killed in coal mine explosion in Pakistan
entries.snippet: Several miners remain unaccounted for following the Balochistan coal mine blast, with authorities saying the explosion was likely due to the build up of methane gas.

entries.title: Indonesia: Pilot faces death penalty after drugs found in suitcase
entries.snippet: A Malaysian Airlines pilot tested positive for cocaine and meth after flying a passenger jet into Jakarta, with Indonesian authorities finding over 70,000 ecstasy pills in his suitcase.

entries.title: Epstein files: How victims remain exposed to identification
entries.snippet: US officials vowed to revise redactions after files exposed information that identified survivors of sexual abuse by Jeffrey Epstein and his associates. A DW investigation found that sensitive information remains online.
